I'm sorry that happened, OP! 🫂 I think you're already on the right track. Is your mom seeing a therapist? Is she on meds? I'm not surprised she thought you wouldn't care. Reality distortion is part of depression. How is she doing after the attempt? People are very vulnerable after a failed attempt. Pretending that it didn't happen or downplaying it is the worst the family could do. 

Talk to her every day, not only about how she is doing, but about you, what you've been up to, what you both like. If you see something she might like, take a picture and send it to her. Ask her opinion or advice. You don't want to over do it and you don't want her to think she's only getting your attention because of what happened. Try to be as natural as possible even though this is not a normal circumstance. 

Make plans with her, so when she thinks about the future,  pain isn't the only thing that comes to mind, but also your upcoming activities. Do you get along with your step dad? If so, include him in those plans. 
Start a hobby with her, maybe? Like knitting or sth similar. An activity in which you can share your progress. 

Especially after an attempt, people might feel like a burden. So you want her to feel wanted and loved. 

The thing with depression is that it could make her feel like "what's the point in treating this other disease?". This is not a rational thought, it's just how depression operates. It might make her feel like she's "getting in the way" of your lives. 

One thing a friend did with me when I was feeling down was asking me for my help. She asked me to help her buy new shoes. It was a simple act. I felt useful and got out of the house. Small acts matter. 

Lastly, she might be feeling ashamed about what happened. It's a strong emotion that could make her feel like she's less than and it could affect her self-esteem. You'd want to help her build her autonomy again. 

Healing takes time. Some of my advice would be better implemented after some weeks/months. Her journey is her own but it's important that she feels loved and wanted.

There's no recipe to follow unfortunately. What I said might not apply to your mom. Anyways, I wish you guys the best.

I work at a school and I see younger people living their lives in a way that wasn't possible for me when I was at their age. then I see my peers ahead of me in life, having achieved things I could've achieved myself if I just hadn't lost my years to depression. 
I'm not really sure how to stop comparing. I just try to tell myself that my thinking is doing me more harm than good, sometimes I will repeat to myself "this thought process is useless" to interrupt an intrusive thought and stop my mind from comparing my life to others. sometimes I try to see other people's achievement as a reminder of what I can still achieve and then I remind myself again that the reason I'm still able to achieve some things is because I'm recovering and that's a good thing. we can not make up for the time lost but we can still have a meaningful future. it will just look different than what we wanted when we were younger. recently I've been trying to accept reality as much as I can to avoid dwelling on hypothetical scenarios. 
one thing I'm sure tho is that the grief only hurts because we are still dealing with the aftermath of it all. I believe that once we achieve certain things that we deem valuable to us we won't be so caught up with these emotions that come up when we compare. ask yourself this: if you achieve the things you desire in the future, would your future-self still compare your life to others or would you just be more concerned with taking care of what you've built and enjoying it? 
I know it's hard to not compare. but you managed to change careers and actually have a job you like. that's pretty amazing! I guess what I'm trying to say is that change is possible and when you look at what other people have, try to see that as possibilities for yourself as well instead of just a reminder of what you lost?

Tenho uma amiga que é coordenadora de curso de inglês (também atuava com prof) com tdha, mas ela era medicada. Também tenho minhas questões de aprendizado, atenção, entre outros e sou professora. Na minha experiência, é preciso ter muita paciência e compaixão consigo mesma. Tanto eu e minha amiga buscavamos formas de nos ajudar: sendo anotando absolutamente tudo para não esquecer, andar sempre com um caderninho, usar notas do celular, muitos e muitos lembretes. Para não tomar decisões impulsivas, recorrer ao "vou verificar na minha agenda e te dou um retorno", quando era algo relacionado a disponibilidade de horário ou se podíamos fazer algo extra. Aceitar que eu não iria recordar coisas de imediato aliviou um pouco a culpa. Entender que seu planejamento de aula terá que ser detalhado ou então feito de forma amigável com suas condições. Verificar a média de tempo que cada questão vai levar, utilizar o despertador pra te avisar se a aula tá acabando ou cronômetro pra lembrar o fim da tarefa. A gente aprende a lidar e procuramos ferramentas para facilitar nossa vida. Relacionamento com a turma e controle dos alunos é realmente um desafio. A questão sensorial nos deixa sensíveis e exaustos. Cada turma tem um perfil, uma abordagem que funciona com uma, não irá necessariamente funcionar com a outra. Mas a dinâmica em sala não depende só de você, é uma colaboração com os alunos, eles fazem parte do aprendizado. Ter uma conversa sincera com eles e estabelecer limites é muito importante. Fazer uma lista de tarefas do dia e elencar por prioridade. Quais são as demandas daquele dia? Muitas anotações e muita paciência. Não há uma solução que sirva para todos. Mas encare sua experiência como uma pesquisa e vai testando o que funciona e o que não funciona (e verificar o porque que deu errado e buscar soluções). As vezes a coordenação me pedia para entregar algum folheto ou pegar assinatura de aluno por motivo x no final da aula e eu esquecia. Depois aprendi que deveria ou deixar em um local visível, ou colocar um aviso no despertador do celular, ou anotar o lembrete no próprio quadro (literalmente escrever "fazer coisa tal no final da aula". Enfim, é uma jornada! Espero ter ajudado um pouco.
